clue.text: Spectacular hole shot by elderly sailor

definitions.meaning: in golf, a hole completed three strokes under par is a rare and spectacular feat with a bird's name
in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner, the old seaman shoots the great seabird with his crossbow

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: a golfing score of three under par, and the bird killed by Coleridge's Ancient Mariner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the golfing term for three under par on a hole, and the seabird the Ancient Mariner shot.

clue.text: A poppy's head concealed insect pest

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so the poppy contributes only its opening letter

parts.note: concealed means hid, the past tense of hide

explanation.surface: A greenfly tucked out of sight in the top of a poppy flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking bugs that gardeners treat as pests, and that is exactly what this insect is.

clue.text: Slam a body of learning in State capital

parts.note: to slam a door is to bang it
lore is a body of traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone criticises a university in an Indian state's chief city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slam' looks like criticism but is the noise BANG. The answer is the capital of Karnataka, a state in southern India.
explanation.definitionFit: This city, now officially Bengaluru, is the seat of government of the Indian state of Karnataka.

clue.text: Will part of plant shut in New Year festival?

indicators.note: something shut in another is enclosed by it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese lunar New Year festival
the stamen is the pollen-bearing male organ of a flower

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether a plant cutting will be locked away during a New Year celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' sits at the front like a verb, but it is the noun for a legal bequest document.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document setting out what happens to a person's estate after death.

clue.text: Comic song? Yes and no

parts.note: the famous aria sung by the clown Canio in Leoncavallo's opera Pagliacci, a clown's song that is nonetheless heartbroken

explanation.walkthrough: The aria 'Vesti la giubba' from Pagliacci is known in English by this title: sung by a clown, so comic in one sense, but full of grief, so not comic at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The English title of the clown's aria is a cryptic fit: it belongs to a comedian yet expresses despair, so it is and is not comic.

clue.text: Sad song in Welsh — contends with translation

indicators.note: translation turns words into a different form, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Welsh-language lament competes once it is translated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with translation' rearranges INWELSHCONTENDS. The answer is Stephen Sondheim's wistful song from A Little Night Music.
explanation.definitionFit: Sondheim's ballad is a melancholy reflection on regret and missed chances, so it counts as a sad song.

clue.text: Having pet around home is lovely!

indicators.note: around means one piece wraps about the other

parts.note: a pup, a young dog, is a typical pet
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone declares that owning a pet at home is delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lovely' is a noun here: a glamorous person whose picture is put on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A lovely, as a noun, is an attractive person, especially one whose photograph is displayed on a wall.

clue.text: Smarten up unduly formal page

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and formal

explanation.surface: A stuffy page boy is told to tidy himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to make oneself neat or groomed, fussing over hair and clothes.

clue.text: It's quickly set up at end of rope

definitions.text: It's quickly set up at end of rope

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: soon means in a short time, quickly

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A hangman's loop is speedily tied at the end of a length of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reads 'quickly' upwards, as a down clue goes, and 'end of' takes the final letter of 'rope'. Read whole, the clue describes a slipknot loop that tightens fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A running knot that tightens is easily made at the tip of a rope, which is what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Make-believe monarch?

parts.note: a claimant to a throne held by someone else, who is a monarch only in their own eyes and those of supporters

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the play on 'make-believe': such a claimant is not a pretend king in a game but someone who claims a throne without holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant such as the Old or Young Pretender asserted a right to the crown, making them a monarch only in make-believe.

clue.text: Cutting tool workmen almost dread

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farmhands

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: awe is reverential dread

explanation.surface: Labourers are nearly afraid of a sharp implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the final E from AWE to leave AW.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw used with one hand for cutting wood is a basic cutting tool.

clue.text: Nasty rumour circulating about high honour

indicators.note: a rumour circulating about something goes round it, so the honour sits inside the rumour

parts.note: noise can mean rumour or talk, as in noises about a takeover
OM is the Order of Merit, a high British honour

explanation.surface: Unpleasant gossip spreads about someone's prestigious award.
explanation.walkthrough: OM, the Order of Merit, is an exclusive British honour in the gift of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially of smells, so it is a synonym of nasty.

clue.text: Crisis involving male lead in RADA production

indicators.note: one thing involving another includes it, so the letter goes inside
a production stages something afresh, so the letters of the London acting academy's initials are rearranged
the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Turmoil surrounds the leading man in a show at the London drama school.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London. 'production' rearranges RADA as DRAA, and 'involving' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is an exciting or turbulent situation, a crisis or fuss, as in making a drama out of something.

clue.text: Follow with composition for violin section

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them
a piece is a musical composition

explanation.surface: A musician follows up with a work written for the violin section of an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violin section' suggests the orchestra's violinists, but it is a part of the instrument itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The tailpiece is the part of a violin, below the bridge, to which the strings are anchored.

clue.text: Pawn official gown, leading to investigation

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
a robe is the gown worn by a judge or official

explanation.surface: A pawned judicial gown sets off an inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: A probe is a thorough inquiry, such as a police or press investigation.

clue.text: Too choppy to work on office document check tod ment

clue.text: Water traded by Italian recalled, lacking a proper document

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the named letter is taken out
recalled means called back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain, and a river is water
dealt means traded, as in dealt in antiques

explanation.surface: River water bought and sold by an Italian is called back, with no proper paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses DEE + DEALT + IT to TITLAEDEED, and 'lacking a' removes the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A title deed is the legal document proving ownership of property, a proper document in the formal sense.

clue.text: Wheels spinning before occupying a minute, different position

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Wheels spinning before occupying a minute, different position': ana(WHEELS) + ERE gives the answer but 'occupying a minute' has no job and gives no letters; likely OCR garble, scan unreadable and no web source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Wheels spinning before occupying a minute, different position

clue.text: Walker went outside and moved faster

indicators.note: outside means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: exited means went out or left
PED, short for pedestrian, is a walker

explanation.surface: A hiker stepped out and hurried along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walker' wants to be a proper name but it is PED, a pedestrian.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite is to speed up a process, so expedited means made to go faster.

clue.text: Public at this point joined in jingoistic old number

parts.note: overt means open and public
here means at this place or point

explanation.surface: The audience at this moment joined in with a patriotic old song.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is George M. Cohan's rousing 1917 song urging Americans to fight in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohan's First World War recruiting song is a famous flag-waving old tune, hence a jingoistic number.

clue.text: Top cop

definitions.meaning: top as an adjective means excellent or first-rate
a police superintendent, a senior officer, is known by a short form

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: an adjective for excellent, and the short form of superintendent, a senior British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means excellent and is also slang for a superintendent, a senior police officer.

clue.text: Where poultice is applied, already heated up

definitions.meaning: a poultice is a hot dressing placed on a skin abscess to draw it
a pot that is bubbling hot, or a situation that is active and lively

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: read literally, the position of a poultice on an abscess; as an idiom, simmering or in progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a poultice goes on top of a skin abscess; idiomatically the phrase means bubbling or at boiling point.

clue.text: Emit a blast, holding musical instruments Lingfield, ment

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Emit a blast, holding musical instruments Lingfield, ment': trailing words 'Lingfield, ment' are OCR noise beyond a letter misread; hidden in 'Emit a blast' but the scan is blank, so the printed clue cannot be confirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: Emit a blast, holding musical instruments Lingfield, ment

clue.text: Worried by each card

parts.note: a ten is a playing card

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about every card dealt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' here is the dog's sense: chewed or gnawed at, as a dog worries a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: To worry something is to bite or gnaw at it, so worried can mean eaten into or consumed.

clue.text: Measurement across, and including diameter

indicators.note: including means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: with can mean and, as in bread with butter

explanation.surface: A dimension taken across a circle, including its diameter.
explanation.definitionFit: Width is the extent of something from side to side, its measurement across.

clue.text: Drink without head is quite useful

indicators.note: without its head means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub drink

explanation.surface: A drink with no froth on top is still fairly worthwhile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without head' suggests a flat pint, but it removes S. SHANDY is a beer and lemonade mix, popular in British pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Handy means convenient or useful; something handy is helpful enough to have around.

clue.text: It's said about part of bypass

indicators.note: about means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: oral means spoken, said aloud rather than written
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: A remark concerns a stretch of road skirting a town.
explanation.walkthrough: An orbital is a ring road circling a city, such as London's M25.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital road runs round a city, which is what a bypass or ring road does.

clue.text: Passion in Old London? How corny!

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Great Wen was William Cobbett's old nickname for London
heat means strong passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: Someone sighs at a sentimental tale of romance in Victorian London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corny' looks like trite, but it means of grain. The Great Wen, a wen being a swelling, was an old nickname for London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheaten means made of wheat, and in British usage corn is a general word for cereal grain such as wheat.

clue.text: Long time before noon

parts.note: a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: A lengthy period passes before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb here: to ache for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to desire it intensely, which is what yearn means.

clue.text: Classic song of years separated by a desert, sadly

indicators.note: two items separated by something have it placed between them

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, so two of them stand for years

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A classic song about years parted by a desert, sung mournfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges A DESERT as ESTERDA, which goes between the two Ys.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles' ballad, written by Paul McCartney, is one of the most recorded songs ever, a true classic.
